com.vector.cfg.automation.api.userinteraction

Interface IUserInteractionApi

  • All Superinterfaces:
    IUserInteractionMessageService

    @PublishedApi(value=ADDITIONS_ALLOWED)
 @PublishedApiDomain(value=AUTOMATION_IF)
public interface IUserInteractionApi
extends IUserInteractionMessageService
    IUserInteractionApi provides API to display messages to the user. Use the IUserInteractionApiEntryPoint to retrieve an instance of IUserInteractionApi.
    The UserInteraction API provides methods to display messages to the user directly. In UI mode the DaVinci Configurator will prompt a message box an will block until the user has acknowledged the message. In console (non UI) mode, the message is logged to the console in a user logger. The user logger will display error, warnings and infos by default. The logger name will not be displayed. The user interaction is good to display information where the user has to respond to immediately. Please use the feature sparingly, because users do not like to acknowledge multiple messages for a single script task execution. The code block userInteractions{} provides the API inside of the block. The following methods can be used:
    • errorToUser()
    • warnToUser()
    • infoToUser()
    • messageToUser(ELogLevel, Object)
    The severity (error, warning, info) will change the display (icons, text) of the message box. No other semantic is applied by the severity.

      • progress

        @PublishedMethod
<T> T progress(java.lang.String message,
                                 groovy.lang.Closure<T> code)
        Updates the progress information for the user with the message, during the code is running.
        If you perform long running operations in a script task, you should display some progress to the user, otherwise the user may cancel the whole execution. The progress API will display the progress of the currently running script task by the information provided by the script code. The method progress(String, Closure) displays the passed message in progress information dialog and executed the code block. So the message is displayed until the code block has finished.
        You could also nest multiple progress() calls. When a progress block is left, the parent progress text will be displayed again.
        Type Parameters:
        T - the return type of the code
        Parameters:
        message - the message to display to the user
        code - the code to execute
        Returns:
        the returned value of the code block

      • progress

        @PublishedMethod
<T> T progress(java.lang.String message,
                                 int totalWork,
                                 groovy.lang.Closure<T> code)
        Updates the progress information for the user with the message, during the code is running.
        The method progress(String, int, Closure) updates the progress information for the user with the message, during the code is running with work ticks.

        It also indicates progress in the progress bar, but you have to set the total amount of work. The total work will be taken from the parent and sets the remaining work for the code block.

        The root script task always starts with totalWork of 1000 ticks, so you have to consume 1000 ticks to fill the progress bar.

        Eclipse API

        You can also use the underlying Eclipse API to fine grain control the progress bar and information data. To do this use the getProgressMonitor() method to retrieve the Eclipse SubMonitor. See also the Eclipse API SubMonitor.setWorkRemaining(int) to scale your own work to different values (also more than 1000 ticks).

        Type Parameters:
        T - the return type of the code
        Parameters:
        message - the message to display to the user
        totalWork - the total work
        code - the code to execute
        Returns:
        the returned value of the code block
